chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Your helping the weak is from the most superior of the charity.'

key_terms.الضَّعِيفَ: The weak (one who is weak or in need)

ai.seo_question: What is considered the best form of charity according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the Prophet’s teaching to the concept of 'sadaqah' as a broad act of benevolence rather than merely obligatory alms. It underscores the Shia emphasis on social solidarity, where aiding the vulnerable is elevated to a supreme spiritual merit, reflecting the Imams' role in clarifying the ethical dimensions of prophetic traditions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Your helping the weak is from the most superior of the charity’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “
The Messenger of Allah O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Your helping a weak person is the best charity.”’
